First and foremost, perfectionism is generally not a very mentally healthy approach to life, so I don't think anyone should expect perfect discipline out of themselves. However, its probably reasonable to assume that striving for perfect discipline is a good way to continue improving oneself. I think the question is conceptually interesting and

Personally, I've been working on getting more disciplined for years and I think I've reached a pretty impressive level. Compared to my past self, I am infinitely more disciplined. However, what I have thus far never been able to do is reach perfect discipline, and maintain it for long periods of time. It seems that even though I can be 100% disciplined for a few days, eventually small failures appear and I eventually return to a baseline level.

I'm sure this isn't a rare phenomenon, and I'm curious to hear what others have to say on the subject. Are humans capable, theoretically or in practice, of consistently being perfectly disciplined over time? If anyone has been able to do so, what can you share about your experience?
